ms.report:
Payment support for USDM:
🎥 Video DEMO 1: Merchant-to-Merchant Transfer (Link) 

This video showcases money transfers using the HydraPay system between merchants. Key functionalities demonstrated:
・Merchant CIP-30 L1 signatures through browser wallets for deposit and withdrawal actions. Each deposit and withdrawal is gated through cryptographic signatures verified on-chain, ensuring that only authorized merchants can initiate balance-affecting actions. This establishes a robust trust model within the Layer 2 network while preserving decentralization principles.
・Merchant-to-merchant transfers in L2. Funds can be transferred seamlessly between merchant accounts, facilitated entirely within the Hydra ledger. 
・Native assets integration and demonstration using ADA and USDM. All balances and transactions in this demo are denominated in ADA and/or USDM. This demonstrates our multi-asset capability on Hydra and lays the foundation for broader support of tokens within decentralized commerce workflows. 

🎥 Video DEMO 2: Mobile Client to Merchant Payment (Link) 

This demonstration shows end-to-end mobile payment through a contactless BLE-enabled terminal. Details include:
・This demonstration showcases a fully operational payment flow from a mobile client to a merchant using our BLE-enabled terminal, and our hydra payment system.
・Given the current lack of support for development in native environments and mobile operating systems, the client initiates a USDM deposit by transferring funds to a designated Layer 1 contract address. To facilitate contract interaction and preserve UX continuity, administrative signing is performed on behalf of the user. This step simulates client-side contract execution pending deeper mobile support.

Building in public (full milestone report):

During this milestone we faced two main challenges.
First, Hydra went through several iterations up to Hydra 1.0 (September 2025), which required us, together with TxPipe as our main contractor, to revisit and rework significant parts of the codebase, plus additional internal work and coordination.
Second, the Chang hardfork introduced changes on Cardano that forced us to review all the libraries and SDKs we rely on, patch our own code, and coordinate with SDK maintainers to update specific components. We knew about this beforehand and it was part of the expected work of the milestone.
Additionally, for a particular set of transactions that must happen inside Hydra, we contracted the Atlas transaction builder library team to adapt their tooling to Hydra.
